subject: SCI
title: Science 8 (Integrated)
description: Integrated Grade 8 science following the California preferred integrated model. Students investigate forces, motion and energy; gravity and the solar system; waves and information technology; Earth's history and the fossil record; heredity; and natural selection. Each week includes a hands-on investigation with household materials, data analysis, and written scientific explanations, ending with an engineering design capstone.
framework: California Next Generation Science Standards (CA NGSS); 2016 California Science Framework (Preferred Integrated Model, Grade 8)

standards.MS-PS2-1: Apply Newton's Third Law to design a solution to a problem involving the motion of two colliding objects.
standards.MS-PS2-2: Plan an investigation showing that the change in an object's motion depends on the sum of the forces on it and its mass.
standards.MS-PS2-4: Argue from evidence that gravitational interactions are attractive and depend on the masses of interacting objects.
standards.MS-PS3-1: Construct and interpret graphical displays of data describing the relationships of kinetic energy to mass and to speed.
standards.MS-PS3-2: Develop a model showing that changing the arrangement of objects interacting at a distance changes the potential energy stored.
standards.MS-PS3-5: Argue that when the kinetic energy of an object changes, energy is transferred to or from the object.
standards.MS-PS4-1: Use mathematical representations to describe a simple model for waves including how amplitude relates to energy.
standards.MS-PS4-2: Develop and use a model describing how waves are reflected, absorbed, or transmitted through various materials.
standards.MS-PS4-3: Integrate information to support the claim that digitized signals are a more reliable way to encode and transmit information than analog signals.
standards.MS-ESS1-1: Develop and use a model of the Earth-sun-moon system to describe cyclic patterns of lunar phases, eclipses, and seasons.
standards.MS-ESS1-2: Develop and use a model describing the role of gravity in the motions within galaxies and the solar system.
standards.MS-ESS1-3: Analyze and interpret data to determine scale properties of objects in the solar system.
standards.MS-ESS1-4: Construct an explanation from rock-strata evidence for how the geologic time scale organizes Earth's 4.6-billion-year history.
standards.MS-LS3-1: Develop and use a model of why mutations in genes may have harmful, beneficial, or neutral effects on the structure and function of the organism.
standards.MS-LS3-2: Model why asexual reproduction produces genetically identical offspring and sexual reproduction produces genetic variation.
standards.MS-LS4-1: Analyze and interpret data for patterns in the fossil record documenting the existence, diversity, extinction, and change of life forms.
standards.MS-LS4-2: Explain anatomical similarities and differences among modern and fossil organisms to infer evolutionary relationships.
standards.MS-LS4-3: Analyze pictorial data to compare patterns of similarity in embryological development across species.
standards.MS-LS4-4: Explain how genetic variations of traits in a population increase some individuals' probability of surviving and reproducing.
standards.MS-LS4-5: Gather and synthesize information about technologies that have changed the way humans influence the inheritance of desired traits.
standards.MS-LS4-6: Use mathematical representations to explain how natural selection may lead to increases and decreases of specific traits over time.
standards.MS-ETS1-1: Define the criteria and constraints of a design problem.
standards.MS-ETS1-2: Evaluate competing design solutions using a systematic process.
standards.MS-ETS1-3: Analyze data from tests to determine similarities and differences among design solutions and combine their best characteristics.
standards.MS-ETS1-4: Develop a model to generate data for iterative testing and modification of a proposed design.

units.title: Forces and Motion
units.big_idea: An object's motion changes only when the forces on it are unbalanced, and every force comes in an equal and opposite pair.

units.title: Energy in Motion and at a Distance
units.big_idea: Kinetic energy depends on mass and speed; energy stored in fields changes with position and transfers whenever motion changes.

units.title: Gravity and the Solar System
units.big_idea: Gravity, which depends on mass, shapes orbits, tides, and the cyclic patterns we see in the sky.

units.title: Waves, Light, and Information
units.big_idea: Waves carry energy and information; materials reflect, absorb or transmit them, and digital signals carry information reliably.

units.title: Earth's History and the Fossil Record
units.big_idea: Rock layers and fossils record 4.6 billion years of Earth and life history and reveal shared ancestry.

units.title: Heredity: Genes and Reproduction
units.big_idea: Genes code for proteins that shape traits; reproduction and mutations create variation, and people now influence inheritance with technology.

units.title: Natural Selection and Adaptation
units.big_idea: Variation plus environmental pressures change trait frequencies in populations over generations.

units.title: Engineering Design Capstone
units.big_idea: Engineers define problems, test competing solutions, and iterate using data.

objectives: Describe motion using position, distance, speed and a frame of reference
Make and interpret distance-time graphs

days.title: Science notebook & frames of reference
days.work: Set up a science notebook; observe a toy car rolling past from two viewpoints and write how each observer would describe its motion.

days.title: Measuring speed
days.work: Mark 0.5 m intervals with tape, time a toy car over 3 m, and calculate average speed in m/s for 3 trials.

days.title: Distance-time graphs
days.work: Graph your toy-car data and walking data; interpret steepness as speed and flat segments as stopping.

days.title: Velocity and direction
days.work: Use the PhET 'Forces and Motion: Basics' motion screen to compare speed and velocity; record 3 observations.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on speed calculations and interpreting 4 distance-time graphs; write a one-paragraph summary of the lab.

weeks.assessment: Speed lab data table and graph plus Friday quiz.

objectives: Identify contact and non-contact forces
Calculate net force and predict motion from balanced or unbalanced forces
materials: small spring scale or rubber band 'force meter'

days.title: Pushes and pulls
days.work: Draw force diagrams (arrows) for 6 everyday situations such as a book on a table and a tug-of-war.

days.title: Net force
days.work: Use the PhET Forces and Motion tug-of-war screen to predict and test motion for 8 combinations of forces; record net force calculations.

days.title: Friction investigation
days.work: Pull a shoe across carpet, tile and wood with a rubber-band force meter; measure stretch and rank surfaces by friction.

days.title: Analyzing friction data
days.work: Graph friction results, identify variables held constant, and write a claim-evidence-reasoning (CER) paragraph.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on net force diagrams and the friction CER.

weeks.assessment: Friction CER and force diagram quiz.

weeks.topic: Newton's second law: force, mass and acceleration
objectives: Plan an investigation of how mass and force affect acceleration
Use F = ma qualitatively and quantitatively
materials: coins or washers for added mass

days.title: Inertia
days.work: Do the coin-on-card flick and tablecloth-style demonstrations; explain Newton's first law in your notebook.

days.title: Planning the investigation
days.work: Write a plan to test how added mass changes the speed of a car released down a ramp: question, variables, procedure, data table.

days.title: Carrying out the investigation
days.work: Run 3 trials each with 0, 2, 4 and 6 washers taped to the car; calculate average times and speeds.

days.title: Force & mass math
days.work: Graph your results; solve 8 F = ma problems and relate the math to your data.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a lab report conclusion and take a quiz on Newton's first and second laws.

weeks.assessment: Lab report on mass and motion; quiz.

objectives: Identify action-reaction force pairs
Explain collisions using Newton's third law

days.title: Balloon rocket
days.work: Build a balloon rocket on a string line; measure distance traveled for small, medium and large balloon inflations and identify the force pair.

days.title: Force pairs
days.work: Label action-reaction pairs in 8 scenarios (swimmer, rocket, rowing, hammer and nail) and explain why the pairs do not cancel.

days.title: Marble collisions
days.work: Roll marbles of the same and different sizes along a ruler groove into each other; record and explain what happens after collisions.

days.title: Collision analysis
days.work: Watch slow-motion crash test footage and explain the forces on the car and the dummy; connect to seatbelts and airbags.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on Newton's third law; draw force-pair diagrams for two collisions.

objectives: Define criteria and constraints for a collision-protection device
Test, compare and improve designs using Newton's third law

days.title: Define the problem
days.work: Write criteria and constraints for a device that protects an egg in a 2-meter drop or a cart crash, using limited materials.

days.title: Design & decision matrix
days.work: Sketch 3 designs and choose one with a decision matrix scoring cost, mass and expected protection.

days.title: Build & test
days.work: Build the prototype and test it; record results and observe how the device increases collision time.

days.title: Iterate
days.work: Redesign based on test data, retest, and compare results with a family member's design.

days.title: Unit 1 test
days.work: Unit test on motion, forces and Newton's laws; submit engineering notebook pages.

weeks.assessment: Engineering notebook rubric and Unit 1 test.

objectives: Describe kinetic energy as energy of motion
Graph how kinetic energy depends on mass and speed
materials: marbles or balls of different masses
paper cup with a door cut in it

days.title: Energy of motion
days.work: Brainstorm examples of moving objects and rank them by kinetic energy; read an introduction to KE = 1/2 m v^2.

days.title: Mass and kinetic energy
days.work: Roll balls of different mass from the same ramp height into a cup; measure how far the cup slides as evidence of energy.

days.title: Speed and kinetic energy
days.work: Roll the same ball from increasing ramp heights (faster speeds) and measure cup distance.

days.title: Graphing KE
days.work: Graph both data sets and use KE calculations to explain why doubling speed has a bigger effect than doubling mass.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on interpreting KE graphs and 5 KE calculations.

objectives: Model gravitational, elastic and magnetic potential energy
Explain how changing distance between interacting objects changes stored energy

days.title: Gravitational PE
days.work: Drop a ball from 3 heights onto a tray of flour or sand and measure crater size; model energy stored by height.

days.title: Elastic PE
days.work: Launch rubber bands stretched 5, 10 and 15 cm and measure distance traveled; relate stretch to stored energy.

days.title: Magnetic PE
days.work: Measure the distance at which a paper clip jumps to a magnet; model how arrangement changes stored energy with diagrams.

days.title: Modeling systems
days.work: Draw energy models (before/after diagrams) for a roller coaster, bow and arrow and two magnets.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on potential energy types and models.

weeks.assessment: Potential energy model diagrams and quiz.

objectives: Track energy transfer between kinetic and potential forms
Argue that changes in kinetic energy mean energy was transferred
materials: foam pipe insulation cut in half (or paper track)

days.title: Energy Skate Park
days.work: Use the PhET Energy Skate Park sim to observe energy bar graphs as the skater moves; record 3 patterns.

days.title: Pendulum lab
days.work: Build a string-and-washer pendulum and observe energy changes; explain why it eventually stops (thermal energy).

days.title: Marble roller coaster
days.work: Build a foam-tube coaster with a loop; find the minimum starting height for the marble to complete the loop.

days.title: Argument writing
days.work: Write a CER argument: 'When the marble slows down, where did its energy go?' using evidence from labs.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Peer/parent review of CER using a rubric; quiz on energy transfer.

weeks.assessment: Roller coaster design and energy CER.

objectives: Analyze energy transfers in collisions
Synthesize unit learning about kinetic and potential energy

days.title: Bounce test
days.work: Drop tennis, rubber and clay balls from 1 m; measure rebound heights and calculate the percent energy retained.

days.title: Slow-motion analysis
days.work: Film collisions in slow motion and identify where energy goes (sound, heat, deformation).

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Create a concept map connecting force, motion, kinetic energy, potential energy and energy transfer.

days.title: Practice assessment
days.work: Answer 3 data-analysis questions using kinetic energy graphs.

days.title: Unit 2 test
days.work: Unit test on energy.

weeks.topic: Gravity is attractive and depends on mass
objectives: Use evidence to argue that gravity depends on mass and distance
Compare weight on different planets

days.title: Gravity well model
days.work: Stretch a sheet or fabric and place heavy and light balls on it; roll marbles to model gravitational attraction.

days.title: Data on gravity

days.title: Review & check

objectives: Model the cause of lunar phases
Explain solar and lunar eclipses

days.work: In a dark room, hold a ball on a pencil at arm's length around a lamp to model all 8 phases; sketch each.

days.title: Phase sequence

days.title: Eclipses

days.title: Review & check

Analyze day-length and sunlight-angle data

days.work: Write what causes seasons; examine Earth-Sun distance data showing Earth is closest to the Sun in January.

days.work: Shine a flashlight straight down and at an angle on graph paper; count squares lit to compare energy concentration.

days.title: Day-length data
days.work: Graph monthly day length for your city and a city in the Southern Hemisphere; describe patterns.

days.title: Modeling the orbit

days.title: Review & check

objectives: Explain how gravity keeps planets and moons in orbit
Describe the role of gravity in forming the solar system and galaxies

days.work: Use PhET 'Gravity and Orbits' to turn gravity off and change masses; record effects on orbits.

days.title: Review & check

objectives: Analyze data on sizes and distances of solar system objects
Build scale models and explain their limitations

days.title: Size data

days.work: Explain why one model cannot show both sizes and distances to the same scale; calculate a scale where Earth is a peppercorn.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Review gravity, moon phases, eclipses, seasons and scale with a self-made study guide.

days.title: Unit 3 test
days.work: Unit test on gravity and the solar system.

objectives: Identify wavelength, amplitude and frequency

days.title: Making waves
days.work: Use a Slinky or rope to make transverse and longitudinal waves; sketch and label each.

days.title: Wave on a String

days.work: Drop a pebble from different heights into a pan of water and observe wave height; relate amplitude to energy.

days.title: Review & check

objectives: Model how light interacts with materials

days.work: Quiz with ray diagrams for reflection and refraction.

days.title: Semester review: space & waves

days.title: Semester 1 exam

objectives: Compare analog and digital signals

days.title: Superposition

days.title: Cross-cutting relationships
days.work: Order events in 4 rock-layer diagrams with intrusions and faults.

days.title: Index fossils
days.work: Correlate layers from three 'sites' using index fossils.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: sequence events in two geologic cross sections.

coins or M&Ms for half-life model

days.title: Eras and extinctions

days.title: Absolute dating
days.work: Model radioactive half-life by shaking coins and removing 'decayed' ones; graph the results.

days.title: Explanation

days.title: Review & check

objectives: Analyze fossil data for patterns of diversity, extinction and change

days.title: Fossil gallery

days.work: Quiz interpreting fossil data tables.

objectives: Compare homologous and analogous structures

days.title: Chicken wing dissection

days.title: Cladograms

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on homologous and analogous structures and cladograms.

objectives: Compare embryos across species

days.title: Unit review

days.title: Unit 5 test
days.work: Unit test on Earth's history and evidence for common ancestry.

objectives: Compare asexual and sexual reproduction
Explain why sexual reproduction produces variation

days.work: Compare budding, binary fission and fragmentation with sexual reproduction using a Venn diagram.

objectives: Explain that genes on chromosomes come in pairs from two parents

objectives: Describe DNA structure and how genes code for proteins
